title: Definitions register: legal and statistical meanings of 'semiconductor', 'leading-edge', 'mature/legacy' and 'advanced' chips across jurisdictions
why_it_matters: Laws, subsidy programmes, export controls and market statistics each draw the industry's boundaries differently (what counts as a 'semiconductor', a 'legacy' chip or an 'advanced computing' chip). If the atlas mixes these definitions, figures and rules will be compared that do not measure the same thing.
questions: How do WSTS, SIA, SEMI, Gartner and the OECD define the scope of the semiconductor industry (products included and excluded, e.g. displays, solar cells, passives)?

How do the main laws define 'semiconductor' and related terms: US CHIPS Act (15 U.S.C. 4651), EU Chips Act (Regulation (EU) 2023/1781) Article 2, Japan's Economic Security Promotion Act designation, Korea's K-Chips Act and Semiconductor Special Act, India's ISM scheme guidelines?

Where is the line between 'leading-edge', 'mature' and 'legacy' drawn in each policy instrument (e.g. 28nm threshold in CHIPS Act NOFOs and the USTR Section 301 legacy-chip investigation), and how is node naming handled?
How are 'advanced computing' and 'supercomputer' items defined in US export controls (ECCN 3A090/4A090, total processing performance and performance density thresholds)?
Which definitions determine the numbers most often quoted in the atlas, and which figures therefore cannot be compared?
subquestions: Does any statute define 'foundational' or 'legacy' chips by function rather than node?
Do Chinese policies (State Council Document No. 4 of 2020) define IC enterprises by linewidth for tax relief, and with what thresholds?
How do the definitions treat compound semiconductors, photonics and MEMS?
primary_sources: CHIPS Act of 2022 definitions, 15 U.S.C. 4651 (uscode.house.gov)
Regulation (EU) 2023/1781 (European Chips Act), Article 2 definitions (EUR-Lex)
15 CFR Part 774 Supplement No. 1, ECCN 3A090 and 4A090 (eCFR)
USTR Section 301 investigation of China's legacy chips (Federal Register notice, December 2024) (to verify)
CHIPS Program Office NOFO definitions of leading-edge and mature-node facilities (NIST)
China State Council Guo Fa [2020] No. 8 IC and software industry policy (to verify number)
WSTS product classification / Blue Book definitions
Japan METI designation of semiconductors as a specified critical product under the Economic Security Promotion Act (to verify)
secondary_sources: Congressional Research Service reports on semiconductor definitions
open_questions: Keep statistical codes (NAICS/HS) out of scope: RU-0009 covers them.
Output: one comparison table of definitions with claim ids, feeding every market-size and regulation unit.

title: Global chip market time series 1986-2026: WSTS totals by product category and by region of sale
why_it_matters: Almost every other number in the atlas is compared against the size of the chip market. We need one clean, dated series of the reference statistic (WSTS), split by product type and by the region where chips are billed, with clear notes on what it does and does not count.
questions: What is the annual worldwide semiconductor market (WSTS, USD, nominal) for 1986-2025, and the latest WSTS forecast for 2026-2027?
What are the annual splits by WSTS product category (discretes, optoelectronics, sensors, analog, micro, logic, memory) over the same period?
What are the annual splits by region of sale (Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific) and how has the Asia Pacific share evolved?
What does 'region of sale' measure (billing location of the customer's receiving site) and why does it not indicate where chips are made or used?
How much of year-on-year change in 2017-2018, 2021-2022 and 2024-2026 came from memory prices?
subquestions: Which companies report to WSTS and what share of the market is estimated for non-members?
Where are China's sales counted within Asia Pacific, and does SIA publish a China split?
How large are revisions between first release and final Blue Book figures?
primary_sources: WSTS Historical Billings Report (wsts.org, free XLSX with monthly data by region since the 1980s)
WSTS semi-annual forecast releases (spring and autumn)
SIA monthly Global Sales Report press releases
SIA Factbook 2025 and 2026 State of the Industry report
JEITA's Japanese-language WSTS releases (jeita.or.jp)
secondary_sources: Gartner and Omdia annual market press releases for cross-checks
open_questions: prereq: RU-0002 methodology; record which WSTS vintage each figure comes from.
End-use splits are in RU-0008; do not duplicate.

title: Market forecasts and their track record: 2026-2030 outlooks (incl. the 'US$1 trillion by 2030' claim) versus actual outcomes
why_it_matters: Investment and policy decisions lean on forecasts that the industry's own history shows are often wrong at turning points. Knowing who forecasts what, on which basis, and how accurate they have been tells readers how much weight to give the headline projections.
questions: What do WSTS, SIA, SEMI, Gartner, IDC, Omdia, TechInsights and McKinsey forecast for chip revenue in 2026-2030, and what assumptions (AI capex, memory prices, units) drive them?
Who first made the 'US$1 trillion by 2030' projection, when, and how have its date and basis moved?
How accurate were WSTS autumn forecasts for the following year, compared with actuals, over 2000-2025 (especially at turning points in 2001, 2009, 2019, 2023)?
Which forecasts are for chip revenue and which include equipment, materials or systems, so that they are not comparable?
subquestions: How do forecasters split price vs volume for memory in 2026?
Are there published bear-case scenarios, and what triggers them?
primary_sources: WSTS forecast releases archive (wsts.org, historic spring/autumn forecasts)
WSTS Historical Billings Report (actuals)
SEMI equipment and fab forecasts (press releases)
SIA State of the Industry reports 2023-2026
secondary_sources: Gartner, IDC, Omdia, TechInsights forecast press releases
Financial press coverage of forecast revisions
open_questions: prereq: Global chip market time series 1986-2026 (new unit in this batch).
Cycle drivers are RU-0181 and AI-capex sustainability is RU-0206; this unit only assesses forecasts and their accuracy.

title: Product taxonomy and segment sizes: WSTS product classes and sub-classes, ASSP vs ASIC vs general-purpose, and how publishers map to each other
why_it_matters: Chips are not one market: memory, processors, analog and power chips have different buyers, economics and competitors. A shared product taxonomy with sizes for each segment is needed before any competitive or business-model analysis can be done per segment.
questions: What are the WSTS product classes and sub-classes (e.g. MOS micro: MPU, MCU, DSP; logic: ASSP, ASIC, general-purpose logic, FPGA; memory: DRAM, NAND, other) and their revenue for 2020-2025?
How do Gartner, Omdia and TechInsights taxonomies differ (e.g. application-specific vs general-purpose, 'data-center GPU/AI accelerator' categories), and how do they map to WSTS?
Where do AI accelerators, custom ASICs, HBM, image sensors and power discretes (SiC/GaN) sit in each taxonomy?
How large is each segment by revenue and, where published, by units and average selling price?
What share of revenue is at leading-edge vs mature nodes (e.g. TSMC revenue by node) and how does this map to product segments?
subquestions: Which sub-segments are growing faster than the total over 2015-2025?
Which segments are dominated by one or two firms (feed to competition units)?
primary_sources: WSTS product classification and forecast tables by product (wsts.org)
SIA Factbook product-segment charts
TSMC quarterly management reports (revenue by technology node and platform)
Company segment reporting (10-K/20-F) for Nvidia, Micron, TI, Infineon
secondary_sources: Yole Group summaries for power, sensors and imaging
open_questions: End-use (demand) segmentation is RU-0008; capacity by node is RU-0062. This unit is the product/supply-side taxonomy.
prereq: Global chip market time series 1986-2026 (same batch).

title: Chip content per device: semiconductor bill-of-materials share in smartphones, PCs, servers and AI systems
why_it_matters: How much chip value goes into each type of end product links chip demand to device volumes and explains why some end markets matter far more than their unit counts suggest (e.g. one AI server holds more chip value than hundreds of phones).
questions: What is the chip content (USD per device and share of device bill of materials) in a flagship and mid-range smartphone, a notebook PC, a general-purpose server and an AI accelerator server (e.g. 8-GPU system or rack-scale system)?
How has content per device changed from 2015 to 2025, and what drove the change (memory, processors, power)?
How do teardown-based estimates (TechInsights, Counterpoint) compare with top-down estimates (WSTS end-use divided by device shipments)?
Which chip types make up the content in each device category?
subquestions: Automotive content per vehicle is covered in RU-0188; reuse its figures only for comparison.
primary_sources: Company investor presentations giving content-per-device (e.g. Qualcomm, Micron, Nvidia) (to verify)
IDC / Gartner device shipment press releases for denominators
SEC filings of device makers where component costs are disclosed (to verify)
secondary_sources: TechInsights and Counterpoint teardown cost estimates (public summaries)
Academic or analyst papers on AI server cost breakdowns
open_questions: prereq: Product taxonomy and segment sizes (same batch).
AI accelerator cost stack is RU-0103; this unit focuses on device-level chip content, not accelerator internals.

title: Company rankings and market concentration: top chip vendors and their shares, 2000-2025
why_it_matters: Who leads the chip market, and how concentrated it is, has changed sharply (Intel and Samsung at the top for decades, Nvidia first in 2024-2025). A consistent ranking series with concentration measures is the base layer for every competitive analysis.
questions: What are the top 10-25 chip vendors by revenue each year 2000-2025 according to Gartner, Omdia (IHS/iSuppli) and TechInsights (IC Insights), and where do their rankings disagree?
What are the top-5 and top-10 shares and a Herfindahl index of the total market over time?
Which companies entered or left the top 10 and why (mergers, spin-offs, memory cycles, AI)?
How do rankings treat foundries (excluded) and captive chips (e.g. Apple, hyperscalers) and how does that change the picture?
How does the ranking change if measured by company-reported semiconductor segment revenue from filings rather than analyst estimates?
subquestions: Gartner 2025 ranking puts Nvidia first; how do Omdia and TechInsights rank 2025?
Which top-25 vendors are headquartered in each country?
primary_sources: Gartner annual semiconductor revenue press releases (e.g. 12 January 2026 release on 2025 revenue)
Company annual reports and 10-K/20-F semiconductor segment revenue (for cross-check)
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix business reports (DART)
secondary_sources: Omdia and TechInsights ranking press releases
Financial press coverage of annual rankings
open_questions: prereq: Global chip market time series 1986-2026 (same batch).
Leadership-by-country is in the geography unit on company headquarters.

title: Memory market structure: DRAM, NAND and HBM shares by firm and country, including CXMT and YMTC
why_it_matters: Memory is about a quarter to a third of chip revenue and is controlled by very few firms; China's CXMT and YMTC are the first new entrants in decades. Who holds what share, and how fast Chinese makers are growing, drives prices, trade policy and supply risk.
questions: What are DRAM, NAND and HBM revenue shares by company per year 2015-2025 (Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, Kioxia, Western Digital/SanDisk, Solidigm, CXMT, YMTC, Nanya, Winbond)?
What are shares by wafer capacity (wafer starts per month) and by bit output, and how do they differ from revenue shares?
What is the country split of memory production and of memory-company headquarters?
How large are CXMT and YMTC now (capacity, revenue, technology level), and what limits them (export controls, Entity List, equipment access)?
How concentrated is HBM supply by vendor and qualification status with major AI chip buyers?
subquestions: What share of NAND is made by the Kioxia/SanDisk joint venture fabs?
Are there public figures for CXMT revenue in IPO filings (to verify)?
What are specialty/niche memory makers (NOR, SRAM, MRAM) and their shares?
primary_sources: Samsung Electronics and SK hynix annual business reports (DART)
Micron 10-K
Kioxia and SanDisk annual reports / securities filings
CXMT prospectus to Shanghai Stock Exchange STAR Market (to verify)
US BIS Entity List entries for YMTC and CXMT-related parties (Federal Register)
secondary_sources: TrendForce and Omdia market-share press releases
open_questions: Do not repeat memory pricing (RU-0018) or memory history (RU-0012); this unit is current structure and shares.
prereq: Company rankings and market concentration (same batch).

title: Data-centre compute competition: AI accelerators (GPU vs custom ASIC), server CPUs (x86 vs Arm) and networking silicon
why_it_matters: Data-centre chips are now the largest and most profitable segment. Whether Nvidia's lead holds against AMD, custom chips from cloud companies and Chinese alternatives shapes where money flows across the whole chain, from foundry to HBM to packaging.
questions: What are the revenue and unit shares of data-centre AI accelerators by vendor (Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Broadcom- and Marvell-built custom ASICs, Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Huawei Ascend, Cambricon) for 2022-2025?
What are server CPU shares (Intel, AMD, Arm-based designs from AWS, Nvidia, Ampere, Google, Microsoft) by units and revenue?
Who supplies data-centre networking chips (switch, NIC/DPU, interconnect) and with what shares?
What creates lock-in in this segment (software ecosystems such as CUDA, interconnects, system-level offerings) and how are challengers trying to break it?
How has China's domestic AI-chip market split between foreign (export-licensed) and domestic suppliers since 2023?
subquestions: How should Nvidia's systems and networking revenue be separated from chip revenue for share calculations?
What share of AI accelerator spend is custom ASIC vs merchant GPU, and how do estimates differ?
primary_sources: Nvidia, AMD, Intel, Broadcom and Marvell 10-K/10-Q segment disclosures
Cambricon annual report (Shanghai Stock Exchange)
US BIS rules on advanced computing items (Federal Register) for China-market product context
secondary_sources: Mercury Research CPU share summaries (to verify)
TechInsights, Omdia and Jon Peddie Research public share figures
Financial press on hyperscaler custom chip volumes
open_questions: prereq: Product taxonomy and segment sizes (same batch).
Unit economics of accelerators are RU-0103; business model of custom silicon is RU-0092.

title: Client and mobile processor competition: smartphone application processors, modems, PC CPUs and the Arm vs x86 contest
why_it_matters: Phones and PCs are still the largest unit markets for leading-edge chips. A handful of firms (Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek, Intel, AMD, Samsung, UNISOC, HiSilicon) compete here, and the shift of PCs to Arm-based designs and of Apple and others to in-house modems changes who buys leading-edge wafers.
questions: What are smartphone application-processor shares by vendor (units and revenue) 2019-2025, including HiSilicon's return and UNISOC?
Who supplies cellular modems and RF front-end chips, and how are in-house modem efforts (Apple) changing shares?
What are PC CPU shares (Intel, AMD, Apple, Qualcomm, MediaTek) and how fast are Arm-based PCs growing?
What licences and ecosystems shape entry (x86 cross-licence, Arm architecture licences, Windows on Arm)?
subquestions: Which of these vendors are fabless vs IDM, and which foundries and nodes do they use?
How large is China's domestic share of phone processors?
primary_sources: Qualcomm, Intel, AMD 10-K segment disclosures
MediaTek annual report (TWSE MOPS)
Arm Holdings 20-F (licence and royalty segmentation)
secondary_sources: Mercury Research PC CPU shares (to verify)
open_questions: prereq: Product taxonomy and segment sizes (same batch).

title: Analog, power, microcontroller and discrete competition: shares, Chinese entrants and consolidation
why_it_matters: Analog, power, microcontroller and discrete chips go into cars, factories and every electronic device. The market is less concentrated than processors or memory, dominated by US, European and Japanese IDMs, and is where Chinese makers are expanding fastest at mature nodes, which is the root of 'legacy chip' trade disputes.
questions: What are the revenue shares of the top analog vendors (TI, ADI, Infineon, ST, Skyworks, NXP, onsemi, Microchip, Renesas) and the top-10 concentration for 2015-2025?
What are the shares in microcontrollers (Renesas, NXP, Infineon, ST, Microchip, TI) and in power discretes and modules (Infineon, onsemi, ST, Mitsubishi Electric, Fuji Electric, Toshiba, Vishay)?
Which Chinese firms have gained share (e.g. SG Micro, GigaDevice, StarPower, Silan, Wingtech/Nexperia, BYD Semiconductor) and in which sub-segments?
How did M&A (ADI-Maxim, ADI-Linear, Infineon-Cypress, Renesas-Dialog/Intersil/IDT, TI-National) reshape concentration?
How are SiC and GaN power device shares split (STMicroelectronics, Infineon, Wolfspeed, onsemi, Rohm, Chinese SiC makers)?
subquestions: What share of analog is sold via distribution vs direct in this segment (link to RU-0043)?
Which firms have gone fab-lite and which keep internal 300mm analog capacity?
primary_sources: Company annual reports and 10-K/20-F segment revenue (TI, ADI, Infineon, ST, NXP, onsemi, Microchip, Renesas)
Chinese analog company annual reports on SSE/SZSE (SG Micro, GigaDevice, Silan) (to verify listings)
Infineon investor presentations citing Omdia power and MCU share tables (to verify)
secondary_sources: Omdia and TechInsights public ranking summaries
open_questions: prereq: Product taxonomy and segment sizes (same batch).
Business model of analog IDMs is RU-0093; this unit is market structure only.

title: Other segment competition: FPGAs, image sensors, optoelectronics, MEMS and RF
why_it_matters: Several mid-sized segments have their own leaders and very high concentration (e.g. one company leads image sensors; two firms dominate FPGAs). Covering them completes the competitive map so that no product segment is left without evidence.
questions: What are shares in FPGAs/programmable logic (AMD-Xilinx, Altera, Lattice, Microchip, Chinese makers)?
What are shares in CMOS image sensors (Sony, Samsung, OmniVision/Will Semiconductor, STMicroelectronics, SmartSens)?
Who leads LEDs, laser diodes and optical transceiver chips, and MEMS sensors (Bosch, ST, TDK, Broadcom)?
Who leads RF front-end and filter chips (Qualcomm, Broadcom, Skyworks, Qorvo, Murata)?
subquestions: Which of these segments are included or excluded in WSTS optoelectronics and sensors categories?
primary_sources: Sony Group annual report (Imaging and Sensing Solutions segment)
Lattice, Skyworks, Qorvo 10-K filings
Will Semiconductor annual report (SSE) (to verify)
secondary_sources: Yole Group public summaries for sensors, imaging, MEMS and RF
open_questions: prereq: Product taxonomy and segment sizes (same batch).

title: Sources of durable competitive advantage by segment: scale, process leadership, ecosystems, switching costs and what has overturned leaders
why_it_matters: Understanding why leaders stay leaders (or fall) in each part of the chain is essential to judge whether any position, including a new entrant's, is defensible. This synthesises segment evidence into a small set of tested explanations.
questions: In each major segment and stage (memory, data-centre compute, mobile, analog/power, foundry, OSAT, equipment, EDA, IP), what are the documented sources of advantage: scale economics, process technology, software ecosystems, installed base, qualification lock-in, patents?

Which leaders lost their position between 1990 and 2025 (e.g. Intel in process leadership, Japanese DRAM makers, Qualcomm in some modem markets) and what caused each loss, according to filings and credible studies?
How persistent are market shares in each segment (share mobility over 5- and 10-year windows)?
What entry paths have worked for new entrants (state support, acquisition, niche-first, ecosystem compatibility)?
subquestions: Where do the explanations in academic studies conflict with those in company filings?
primary_sources: Company 10-K 'Competition' and 'Risk factors' sections for segment leaders
Competition-authority merger decisions describing market definitions and barriers (European Commission, SAMR, FTC) (to verify specific cases)
secondary_sources: Academic industrial-organisation studies of semiconductor competition
open_questions: prereq: all segment competition units in this batch (memory, data-centre compute, client/mobile, analog/power, other segments) and Company rankings and market concentration.

title: Participant census method: how to enumerate companies in each role (registries, exchange listings, association member lists, government lists)
why_it_matters: The atlas must cover the whole population of companies, not only famous names. Before enumerating, we need to know which lists exist for each role, how complete they are, and how to combine them without double counting.
questions: Which association member directories exist and are public: SIA, SEMI (member directory), GSA, ESD Alliance, JEITA, SEAJ, KSIA, TSIA, CSIA, ESIA/SEMI Europe, IESA (India), MSIA (Malaysia), SSIA (Singapore), ECIA, ERAI, IDEA, IPC?

Which stock-exchange industry classifications identify listed chip companies (GICS 453010 Semiconductors and 453010 equipment sub-industry, ICB, TWSE semiconductor index, SSE STAR Market IC board, KRX) and how many listed firms fall in each?

Which government lists enumerate firms by role: DMEA Trusted Access Program accredited suppliers, CHIPS award recipients, India ISM approved projects, Japan METI subsidy recipients, China's lists of qualified IC enterprises for tax relief, BIS Entity List entries?
Which commercial or open databases (CSET/ETO, SEMI World Fab Forecast, Crunchbase, TechInsights) can supplement, and what are their licence limits?
What method should the atlas use to assign each company a role (ontology entity types) and headquarters country?
subquestions: How often is each list updated and is it machine-readable?
Which roles have no usable list (candidates for interviews)?
primary_sources: SEMI member directory (semi.org)
DMEA Trusted Access Program Office accredited supplier list (dmea.osd.mil)
ECIA authorised distributor directory (ecianow.org / eciaauthorized.com)
CHIPS for America award announcements (NIST)
India Semiconductor Mission approved projects (ism.gov.in)
SSE STAR Market and TWSE industry listings
GICS sub-industry definitions (MSCI/S&P)
secondary_sources: Crunchbase or PitchBook for private firms (licence limits)
open_questions: Output: a per-role table of enumeration sources with coverage, update frequency and access terms; each role unit below uses it.

title: Enumerate chip companies: IDMs, memory makers, fabless firms and system companies designing chips, by country
why_it_matters: Chip companies are the centre of the industry and the sellers counted in market statistics. We need a systematic list (not just the top 25) of who they are, where they are headquartered, and what they make, including the thousands of smaller fabless firms in China, Taiwan, the US, Europe, Israel and India.
questions: How many chip companies exist in each major country, and by type (IDM, fabless, memory, system company)?
Who are the listed chip companies on each major exchange and what are their revenues (claims from filings)?
How many IC design firms does China have (CSIA IC Design Branch annual count presented at ICCAD) and what is their revenue distribution?
Which notable private and start-up chip companies exist in the US, Europe, Israel, India and China (AI chips, RISC-V, photonics, power)?
Which system companies design chips in-house (hyperscalers, phone and car makers) and for what uses?
subquestions: How many of these companies have revenue above US$100m, US$1bn?
Which firms changed type (IDM to fabless, fab-lite) since 2010?
primary_sources: CSIA IC Design Branch annual report at ICCAD (Wei Shaojun, 'Current Status and Development of China's IC Design Industry', 2024 and 2025)
GSA member list and GSA fabless reports (to verify)
SEC EDGAR SIC 3674 company list
TWSE/TPEx semiconductor sector listings (MOPS)
KRX/DART semiconductor sector filings
SSE STAR Market IC company listings
open_questions: prereq: Participant census method (same batch).
Custom-silicon business model is RU-0092; this unit only enumerates.

title: Enumerate manufacturing-service providers: foundries, OSATs, photomask makers and independent test houses, by country
why_it_matters: Contract manufacturers are fewer but far more capital-intensive. A full list, including small specialty foundries, regional OSATs, merchant mask shops and trusted defence suppliers, shows real capacity options for chip designers and where hidden dependencies sit.
questions: Which foundries exist worldwide (pure-play, IDM foundry businesses, specialty and compound-semiconductor foundries), with headquarters, fab locations and node bands?
Which OSATs and independent test houses exist beyond the top 10 (e.g. in Malaysia, Philippines, Vietnam, China, Korea, Japan, Europe, US)?
Which merchant and captive photomask makers exist (Photronics, Toppan Photomasks, DNP, Hoya, Taiwan Mask, SK-electronics, Chinese mask shops) and who owns captive shops?
Which facilities are accredited by the DMEA Trusted Access Program, and for which categories (foundry, packaging, test, mask, design)?
subquestions: Which foundries and OSATs are on the US Entity List?
Which mask makers can make EUV masks?
primary_sources: DMEA Trusted Access Program accredited supplier list (dmea.osd.mil)
Company annual reports (TSMC, UMC, GlobalFoundries, SMIC, Hua Hong, Tower, ASE, Amkor, JCET, Photronics)
SEMI World Fab Forecast public summaries (fab counts)
US BIS Entity List (Federal Register, 15 CFR 744 Supp. 4)
open_questions: prereq: Participant census method (same batch).

title: Enumerate equipment makers and manufacturing-software vendors, including sub-tier suppliers, by country
why_it_matters: A few large tool makers are well known, but hundreds of smaller equipment, subsystem and factory-software firms serve fabs, and China now has a fast-growing domestic tool industry. A systematic list is needed to judge concentration and alternatives.
questions: Which front-end, back-end and test equipment makers exist in the US, Japan, Netherlands, Korea, China, Germany, Israel and elsewhere, by tool category?

Which firms supply manufacturing software (MES, APC/FDC, yield management, automation) to fabs and OSATs (Applied Materials software, PDF Solutions, Siemens, Critical Manufacturing, KLA, Synopsys, Chinese vendors)?
Which Chinese equipment makers are listed (Naura, AMEC, Piotech, ACM Research, Hwatsing, SMEE (unlisted)) and what are their revenues (claims from filings)?
Which members of SEAJ and SEMI are equipment makers and how many are there?
subquestions: Which equipment makers are on the US Entity List or subject to China's unreliable entity measures?
primary_sources: SEAJ member list (seaj.or.jp)
SEMI member directory
Company annual reports and 10-K/20-F (ASML, AMAT, Lam, TEL, KLA, Advantest, Teradyne, Screen, Kokusai)
China SSE/SZSE annual reports of Naura, AMEC, Piotech (to verify)
open_questions: prereq: Participant census method (same batch).

title: Enumerate materials suppliers and critical-mineral producers: wafers, chemicals, gases, substrates, packaging materials and raw minerals
why_it_matters: Materials supply is spread across many specialised, often Japanese, firms and ultimately rests on a small number of mineral producers, mainly in China. A list of who makes each material, and where, exposes single-source points that headline equipment lists miss.
questions: Which companies supply each SEMI materials category (silicon wafers, photoresists, wet chemicals, specialty gases, CMP slurries/pads, targets, mask blanks, IC substrates, leadframes, bonding wire, mold compounds), with headquarters and plant countries?
Which firms produce and refine the critical minerals used in chips (gallium, germanium, high-purity quartz, tungsten, rare earths, helium, neon) and in which countries?
Which materials suppliers are members of SEMI, JEITA or Japanese materials associations, and how many are there?
Which suppliers have been subject to export restrictions (Japan's 2019 Korea controls on fluorinated polyimide, photoresist and hydrogen fluoride; China's 2023-2025 mineral controls)?
subquestions: Which categories have fewer than three qualified suppliers globally?
primary_sources: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (gallium, germanium, quartz, tungsten, rare earths, helium)
Company annual reports and securities filings (Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic, JSR, TOK, Ibiden, Unimicron)
MOFCOM announcements on gallium/germanium export licensing (2023 No. 23) (to verify number)
SEMI materials market reports (public summaries)
open_questions: prereq: Participant census method (same batch).

title: Enumerate design-enablement providers: EDA vendors, IP licensors and design-service houses, incl. foundry ecosystem partner lists
why_it_matters: Chip design depends on a small group of software and IP firms plus hundreds of design-service and IP start-ups tied into foundry ecosystems. Foundry partner lists and consortium member lists give a systematic view of who these firms are and where they are.
questions: Which EDA vendors exist beyond Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens EDA (e.g. Keysight, Ansys (now Synopsys), Empyrean, Primarius, Semitronix, start-ups) and in which countries?
Which IP licensors exist (Arm, Synopsys IP, Cadence IP, Imagination, CEVA, Alphawave, Rambus, SiFive, Andes, VeriSilicon) and which are members of RISC-V International?

Which design-service houses exist (GUC, Alchip, Faraday, VeriSilicon, Socionext, Sondrel, Indian design-service firms) and which foundry partner programmes list them (TSMC OIP, Samsung SAFE, Intel Foundry Accelerator, GlobalFoundries)?
How many firms are in China's domestic EDA and IP sector, and which are listed?
subquestions: Which design-enablement firms are on the US Entity List?
Which firms left the market or were acquired since 2015?
primary_sources: TSMC Open Innovation Platform partner list (tsmc.com)
Samsung Foundry SAFE partner list (to verify public)
RISC-V International member list (riscv.org)
ESD Alliance member list
Company annual reports and filings (Synopsys, Cadence, Arm, GUC, Alchip, VeriSilicon, Empyrean)
open_questions: prereq: Participant census method (same batch).

title: Enumerate channel intermediaries: authorised distributors, catalogue houses, independent distributors and brokers, by region
why_it_matters: The distribution channel moves a large share of chips to the many smaller buyers, and the open market is where counterfeit risk enters. Knowing who is authorised and who is not is basic to any sourcing, risk or channel analysis.
questions: Who are the largest authorised distributors worldwide and by region (Arrow, Avnet, WPG, WT Microelectronics, Macnica, Future, TTI, Digi-Key, Mouser, Rutronik) and what are their semiconductor revenues (claims from filings)?
Which firms are members of distributor associations (ECIA, IDEA, DMASS in Europe, Japanese and Chinese distributor associations)?
Which independent distributors and brokers are recognised (ERAI membership, IDEA-STD-1010 certification, AS6081 certified) and how many are there?

title: Chip buyers: top purchasers by spend, OEM and EMS/ODM enumeration, and customer concentration of chip suppliers
why_it_matters: A few buyers (Apple, Samsung, hyperscalers, large PC and phone makers, and EMS firms like Foxconn) account for a big share of chip purchases. Who they are and how dependent chip suppliers are on them determines bargaining power and risk.
questions: Who are the top chip buyers by spend (Gartner's annual top-10 semiconductor buyers / design TAM ranking) over 2015-2025?
Which EMS and ODM firms buy chips on behalf of OEMs, and how large are they (Foxconn/Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron, Pegatron, Jabil, Flex, Luxshare, BYD Electronic)?
What customer concentration do chip suppliers disclose (10%-customer disclosures in 10-K/20-F: e.g. Nvidia, Qualcomm, Broadcom, TSMC's top customers)?
How has the buyer mix shifted towards hyperscalers and AI server builders since 2022?
subquestions: Which buyers also design their own chips (link to system companies)?
Which Chinese OEMs are among top buyers and how have export controls affected them?
primary_sources: Gartner annual 'top semiconductor buyers' press releases (gartner.com newsroom)
10-K/20-F customer concentration disclosures (Nvidia, Qualcomm, Broadcom, AMD, Micron, TSMC)
Hon Hai, Quanta, Wistron annual reports (TWSE MOPS)
Jabil and Flex 10-K filings

title: Market share by company headquarters country, 1985-2025, and how it differs from production location
why_it_matters: Saying a country 'has x% of the chip industry' can mean where companies are headquartered, where chips are made, or where they are sold. The HQ-based share (e.g. US firms at about half of sales) is widely quoted but is very different from manufacturing share, and the atlas must keep them apart.
questions: What are the shares of worldwide chip sales by company headquarters (US, South Korea, Japan, Europe, Taiwan, China) for 1985-2025 per SIA/Omdia?
How does the HQ share differ by product segment (e.g. US in logic and analog vs Korea in memory)?
How do HQ shares compare with manufacturing capacity shares and with region-of-sale shares for the same years?
How are foundries treated (excluded from HQ share because their revenue is not chip sales)?
subquestions: When did US share peak and trough, and what explains the 1985-1997 shift?
What share of Chinese domestic demand is supplied by China-headquartered firms?

title: History: origins of the industry, 1947-1980 (transistor, integrated circuit, Silicon Valley, military and space demand, first offshoring)
why_it_matters: The industry's structure (US design leadership, Asian assembly, government as first customer) was set in its first three decades. Knowing where it came from explains why some positions are so persistent.
questions: What were the key inventions and first products (point-contact transistor 1947, integrated circuit 1958-59, planar process, MOS, microprocessor 1971, DRAM 1970) and who made them?
How important were US military and space programmes as early customers and funders (share of IC purchases in the 1960s)?
How did Silicon Valley form (Shockley, Fairchild, 'Fairchildren' spin-outs, Intel)?
When and why did US firms first move assembly to Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines?
What were the market size and leading firms around 1960, 1970 and 1980?
subquestions: What role did Bell Labs' patent licensing (1952 symposium) play in spreading the technology?
primary_sources: US Department of Commerce 1979 report 'A Report on the U.S. Semiconductor Industry' (to verify)
Computer History Museum 'Silicon Engine' timeline (computerhistory.org)
Company histories and archives (TI, Intel)
GAO historical reports (SRC-0047 lists one; others to verify)
open_questions: Labour offshoring details are in RU-0131; technology history is RU-0079. This unit gives the industrial narrative with dated milestones.

title: History: the rise of South Korea and Taiwan (1970s-2010s) - Samsung's memory entry, ITRI, TSMC and UMC, and the state's role
why_it_matters: South Korea and Taiwan went from assembly locations to world leaders in memory and foundry in about two decades. How that happened (state institutes, conglomerates, a new business model) is the main precedent every other country's chip plan cites.
questions: When and how did Samsung, Hyundai (later SK hynix) and LG enter DRAM, and how did they overtake Japanese makers?
What role did Korean government programmes and finance play (e.g. the 1980s VLSI projects, bank lending), per primary or scholarly sources?
How were ITRI, the 1976 RCA technology-transfer deal, UMC (1980) and TSMC (1987) created, and how were they funded (incl. Philips' stake in TSMC)?
How did Taiwan's fabless and OSAT sectors (MediaTek, ASE, SPIL) develop?
What shares of world production did Korea and Taiwan hold in 1990, 2000 and 2010?
subquestions: What role did the 1997-98 Asian financial crisis and the Hyundai-LG merger play?
primary_sources: ITRI official history pages (itri.org.tw)
TSMC 20-F and annual reports (history, founding shareholders)
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix corporate histories and DART filings
Taiwan Executive Yuan / NDC historical policy documents (to verify)
secondary_sources: Academic studies (e.g. Mathews and Cho 'Tiger Technology')
open_questions: Memory consolidation specifics are RU-0012; value-chain disaggregation is RU-0011. This unit is the national-development story.

title: History: the US response to Japan and the US industry 1980-2020 - SEMATECH, trade agreements, Intel's dominance and the fall in US manufacturing share
why_it_matters: The US lost memory to Japan in the 1980s, rebuilt through microprocessors and design, and then saw its share of global manufacturing capacity fall to around a tenth. This period explains current US policy aims (CHIPS Act) and where US strengths lie.
questions: How did the US share of global chip sales and of manufacturing capacity evolve 1980-2020 (e.g. capacity share ~37% in 1990 to ~12% in 2020, per SIA/BCG, to verify)?
What did SEMATECH (1987) do, how was it funded, and what do evaluations conclude about its effect?
How did Intel, TI and others shift from memory to microprocessors and analog, and what drove US firms to go fabless or fab-lite?
Why did new fab investment move to Asia (cost studies, incentives)?
subquestions: How did the 1986 and 1991 US-Japan semiconductor agreements affect US firms (see RU-0151 for the trade policy itself)?
primary_sources: SIA/BCG 'Government Incentives and US Competitiveness in Semiconductor Manufacturing' (2020)
GAO reports on SEMATECH (e.g. GAO/RCED-92-223, to verify)
National Research Council 'Securing the Future: Regional and National Programs to Support the Semiconductor Industry' (2003)
SIA historical sales data
secondary_sources: Irwin, 'Trade Politics and the Semiconductor Industry' (NBER)
open_questions: Trade agreements are covered as policy in RU-0151; this unit covers industrial outcomes.

title: History: Europe's and China's semiconductor paths before 2014 - Philips, Siemens and SGS-Thomson spin-offs; China's 908/909 projects, SMIC and early policy
why_it_matters: Europe's chip firms were reshaped by spin-offs (NXP, Infineon, STMicroelectronics) and its share fell steadily; China's early projects mostly failed until SMIC and a new policy wave. Both histories explain the starting points of today's EU and Chinese chip strategies.
questions: How were Infineon (1999 from Siemens), NXP (2006 from Philips), STMicroelectronics (1987 merger) and Qimonda formed, and what were Europe's shares of world production over 1980-2014?
